findings.description: The installer gates the retry on "not every batched name was unresolvable" (a count comparison) rather than on the trimmed Brewfile being non-empty, using `[ ]` rather than `[[ ]]` per the bash 3.2 rule.
findings.evidence:
run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:128
  if [ "$allow_retry" -eq 1 ] && [ "${#missing_arr[@]}" -lt "${#fetch_arr[@]}" ]; then

Mutant test: replacing that line with `if [ "$allow_retry" -eq 1 ]; then` (the "Brewfile still non-empty" gate the spec warns about) turns the all-unresolvable case RED:
  not ok 2 install-packages: drop-and-retry, all unresolvable reports without retrying
  `[ "$(wc -l <"$BUNDLE_LOG")" -eq 1 ]' failed (line 277)
So that case discriminates the correct gate from the wrong one.

findings.description: Rubric (a): every added case drives the rendered script as a real subprocess with brew stubbed on PATH, reaching no real Homebrew and mutating no machine state.
findings.evidence:
tests/install-failures.bats:24-28 (setup exports a synthetic HOME under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR) and :236, :275, :303, :348 (PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin" run bash "$script").

$ which brew
/opt/homebrew/bin/brew
$ PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" command -v brew
(no output) -> real brew is unreachable on the test PATH; the stub is the only brew.

The only real-$HOME use is chezmoi execute-template for rendering (tests/install-failures.bats:33-37, :52-54), which is read-only and predates this job.

findings.description: Rubric (b): no case proves its claim from a string the stub echoed — the mixed-batch case reads the Brewfile the script itself piped in, and the text assertions use the two-space indent only the script's own summary emits.
findings.evidence:
tests/install-failures.bats:238-242 asserts on $BUNDLE_LOG's line count and on $BUNDLE_DIR/2, which the stub captures via `cat >"$BUNDLE_DIR/$n"` (:224) from the script's own `brew bundle --file=/dev/stdin <<<"$retry_brewfile"` (run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:141). That content is the script's output, not the stub's.

The supporting text assertions (:278-279, :351) match a two-space prefix produced only by `sed 's/^/  /'` at run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:126; the stubs emit names with a single leading space ("Fetching $NAME1, $NAME2").

Mutant test proving teeth: neutralizing the drop loop at run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:137 (retry still fires, dead line never dropped) turns the mixed-batch case RED at line 242 on `assert_not_contains "\"$DROP_NAME\"" "$second"`.

findings.description: Rubric (c): each added case carries the assertion its own clause names, and the invocation logs are per-case rather than shared across cases.

findings.description: One note for the orchestrator, not a defect: the `no extra brew calls` check is green against HEAD's installer, which the dispatch framed as an automatic C-5 failure, but C-2's own text defines that case as a baseline regression guard ("which is what the script does today"), so red at HEAD is impossible without violating C-2, and C-5's rubric (a)-(d) names no such condition.
findings.evidence:
constitution.md:16 — "A run in which `brew bundle` exits 0 makes no `brew info` call and exactly one `brew bundle` call, which is what the script does today."

$ bats -f "no extra brew calls" tests/install-failures.bats   # against HEAD's installer
1..1
ok 1 install-packages: no extra brew calls on a clean run

The same holds for the all-unresolvable case, whose C-1-mandated assertion (log count == 1) HEAD also satisfies; its discriminating power is against a wrongly-gated retry, demonstrated by the mutant above. The two cases that can distinguish a fixed installer both go red at HEAD.

findings.description: The drop-and-retry branch carries an explanation of why it is gated on the count comparison rather than on a non-empty Brewfile — a constraint a reader would otherwise miss, not a paraphrase of the code.
findings.evidence:
run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:129-134
    # At least one batched name resolves, so the registry isn't entirely to blame — drop
    # only the dead lines and give the survivors the run they never got, since
    # installer.rb's fetch phase returns before installing anything at all. Gating on the
    # count comparison (not on whether the trimmed Brewfile is merely non-empty) matters:
    # the fetch batch is a handful of entries out of dozens in the full Brewfile, so
    # "the Brewfile still has lines in it" stays true even when every batched name is dead.

findings.description: The no-third-attempt stop carries its own explanation, citing the issue that ruled out looping the apply.
findings.evidence:
run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:70-74
# Reports one completed `brew bundle` attempt and, the first time only, retries. $log is
# the tee'd output, $status is brew's own exit code (PIPESTATUS, not tee's), and
# $allow_retry is 1 for the initial attempt and 0 for the retry this function may itself
# trigger — #17 already ruled out looping the apply, so a second failure of either phase
# is always just reported, never retried again.

findings.description: The remaining added comments each explain a constraint or a surprising invariant rather than restating the adjacent line, matching the register of run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:30-35 and :62-67 (upstream line citations, issue numbers, incident dates).
findings.evidence:
run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:113-114 — "bash 3.2 renders an empty array as one empty word under set -u, so both expansions below are count-guarded rather than trusted to iterate zero times." (invariant, not a paraphrase)
:152-155 — "$retry_log is unset unless handle_bundle_result actually retries; an unset trap reference just expands empty, so rm -f no-ops on the happy path instead of needing a second trap registration." (verified accurate: retry_log is assigned without `local` at :140, the trap is single-quoted at :157, and the script sets no `set -u`)
:34-35 — "Factored out because #22's retry needs this same read applied to a second log, not just the first." (why the extraction happened)

No added comment paraphrases its own code; I read every `+`-prefixed comment line in `git diff run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl`.
